item.research_question: How can a Pt-based high-entropy alloy be designed and synthesized to achieve superior oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity and stability compared to commercial Pt/C catalysts in acidic media?
item.material_system: PtFeCoNiCu high-entropy alloy (PFCNC-HEA) nanoparticles with atomic ratio 1.0:2.4:1.9:1.8:2.0 and 2 wt% Pt loading
item.processing_route: Impregnation reduction method: metal precursors (Co(acac)2, Fe(acac)3, Ni(acac)2, Cu(acac)2, H2PtCl6·6H2O) dissolved in water/alcohol, mixed with Vulcan XC-72 carbon support, dried at 70 °C, annealed at 700 °C for 30 min under flowing H2/Ar
item.test_conditions: Three-electrode system in 0.1 M HClO4 at room temperature; Accelerated durability test (ADT) 0.6–1.1 V vs RHE for 10k cycles; Chronoamperometry at 0.7 V for 40,000 s; PEMFC with 0.03 mgPt cm−2 cathodic loading at 0.5–2.0 bar O2 pressure
key_findings: Mass activity of 1.738 A mg−1Pt at 0.90 V, which is 15.8 times higher than commercial Pt/C (0.116 A mg−1Pt)
Half-wave potential (E1/2) of 0.88 V, 30 mV higher than Pt/C (0.85 V)
Negligible voltage decay of 3 mV after 10,000 ADT cycles, compared to 33 mV for Pt/C
Maintains 90.23% of initial current after 40,000 s chronoamperometry, surpassing Pt/C (55.34%)
Maximum power density of 1.380 W cm−2 at 2.0 bar O2 pressure with 0.03 mgPt cm−2 loading
Dissolution energy of Fe becomes positive (1.54 eV) in PFCNC-HEA, inhibiting auto-dissolution compared to pure Fe (−0.465 eV)
d-band center of surface Pt atoms downshifts by 0.36 eV relative to pure Pt (111)
Activation barriers for O-O bond scission of ∗OOH reduced to 0.291–0.326 eV on PFCNC-HEA vs 0.717 eV on Pt (111)
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the enhanced performance to the ligand effect causing electron transfer from non-noble metals to Pt, which downshifts the d-band center to optimize oxygen intermediate binding. The high-entropy effect improves thermodynamic stability and inhibits metal dissolution. Additionally, multi-element alloying creates multiple active sites and synergistic interactions that lower the activation barriers for O-O bond scission and facilitate the formation of ∗OOH intermediates.
item.limitations: The synthesis method is biased toward low loading catalysts; increasing metal load causes significant particle size growth.
quotes: It shows remarkable ORR catalytic mass activity of 1.738 A mg−1Pt at 0.90 V, which is 15.8 times higher than that of the state-of-art commercial Pt/C catalyst.

The dissolution energy of Fe in PFCNC-HEA become positive (1.54 eV), in great contrast to the negative value (−0.465 eV) of that in pure Fe metal, demonstrating that the auto-dissolution of Fe is effectively inhibited through the high entropy effect of PFCNC-HEA.
This synthesis method can only be biased toward the preparation of a low loading catalyst. When the metal load is increased, the particle size will grow significantly.

records.text: Paper card. Question: How can a Pt-based high-entropy alloy be designed and synthesized to achieve superior oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity and stability compared to commercial Pt/C catalysts in acidic media?. System: PtFeCoNiCu high-entropy alloy (PFCNC-HEA) nanoparticles with atomic ratio 1.0:2.4:1.9:1.8:2.0 and 2 wt% Pt loading. Processing: Impregnation reduction method: metal precursors (Co(acac)2, Fe(acac)3, Ni(acac)2, Cu(acac)2, H2PtCl6·6H2O) dissolved in water/alcohol, mixed with Vulcan XC-72 carbon support, dried at 70 °C, annealed at 700 °C for 30 min under flowing H2/Ar. Test conditions: Three-electrode system in 0.1 M HClO4 at room temperature; Accelerated durability test (ADT) 0.6–1.1 V vs RHE for 10k cycles; Chronoamperometry at 0.7 V for 40,000 s; PEMFC with 0.03 mgPt cm−2 cathodic loading at 0.5–2.0 bar O2 pressure. Findings: Mass activity of 1.738 A mg−1Pt at 0.90 V, which is 15.8 times higher than commercial Pt/C (0.116 A mg−1Pt); Half-wave potential (E1/2) of 0.88 V, 30 mV higher than Pt/C (0.85 V); Negligible voltage decay of 3 mV after 10,000 ADT cycles, compared to 33 mV for Pt/C; Maintains 90.23% of initial current after 40,000 s chronoamperometry, surpassing Pt/C (55.34%); Maximum power density of 1.380 W cm−2 at 2.0 bar O2 pressure with 0.03 mgPt cm−2 loading; Dissolution energy of Fe becomes positive (1.54 eV) in PFCNC-HEA, inhibiting auto-dissolution compared to pure Fe (−0.465 eV); d-band center of surface Pt atoms downshifts by 0.36 eV relative to pure Pt (111); Activation barriers for O-O bond scission of ∗OOH reduced to 0.291–0.326 eV on PFCNC-HEA vs 0.717 eV on Pt (111). Mechanism: The authors attribute the enhanced performance to the ligand effect causing electron transfer from non-noble metals to Pt, which downshifts the d-band center to optimize oxygen intermediate binding. The high-entropy effect improves thermodynamic stability and inhibits metal dissolution. Additionally, multi-element alloying creates multiple active sites and synergistic interactions that lower the activation barriers for O-O bond scission and facilitate the formation of ∗OOH intermediates.. Limitations: The synthesis method is biased toward low loading catalysts; increasing metal load causes significant particle size growth.. Quote: "It shows remarkable ORR catalytic mass activity of 1.738 A mg−1Pt at 0.90 V, which is 15.8 times higher than that of the state-of-art commercial Pt/C catalyst."
